messages:
alex: FYI customer AcmePay opened an escalation — p95/p99 regressions on streaming endpoints since runtime v2.14.0 rolled yesterday. They see huge TTFB spikes for long generations, but total time sometimes looks OK.

samir: attaching their repro steps and a snippet from their logs. they say first chunk often delayed 1.8–2.2s (used to be <150ms). non-streaming (sync) endpoints don't show the same first-chunk delay for the same payloads.

alex: Repro (from customer):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-open-2.2", "stream":true, "prompt":"long_prompt_repro...repeat 200x"}'
```
They say p99_first_chunk_latency ~2s, p50 ~120ms.

devon: thanks. any correlation with the runtime deploy? v2.14.0 included the chunk coalescing heuristics change (adaptive_flush_window). Might be this.

maria: I pulled customer traces — I can see the streaming path for that tenant getting a delayed flush decision: kernel emits tokens but the flush candidate is dropped into coalesce window for ~1.9s due to our new heuristic that waits for more tokens when `estimated_remaining` is large.

aj: Huh. That matches a bug we discussed — the heuristic used sequence-length est that was biased for long prefix models. In short, for some long prompt distributions we under-estimate the token emission rate so the adaptive window grows and we hold first chunk.

alex: Customer impact: p99 TTFB up — affecting UI perceived latency. They flagged for SLO impact and asked for immediate mitigation.

devon: Immediate options: 1) route their requests to non-streaming (blocking) endpoints as a short-term workaround, 2) set per-tenant override to disable adaptive coalescing (force immediate flush), 3) rollback v2.14.0 canary for streaming path.

samir: Can you confirm non-streaming actually avoids the delay? We saw non-streaming TTFB is low, but total time higher due to buffering. For their app the UX prefers streaming first-byte quickness.

maria: Verified: non-streaming returns a full response only after generation completes but it writes the response earlier on the client once complete — so the visible first byte to their client was earlier in practice for shorter sequences, but for their long sequences streaming should be better, except for this bug.

aj: Quick metric checks I ran: PromQL:
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_first_chunk_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
For that tenant label it jumps from ~0.12 -> ~1.9 after deploy. Also token_emitted_rate per-tenant dropped on the streaming path because emission was gated by flush window.

devon: Proposed immediate mitigation: enable per-tenant config `streaming_immediate_flush: true` which bypasses adaptive coalescing for AcmePay. That should restore previous behavior. I'll prepare a patch for routing flags.

alex: Customer asked for a timeline. Can we do tenant override now?

maria: I can push a routing policy override in the control plane:
```json
{ "tenant_id": "acmepay", "streaming": { "adaptive_coalesce": false, "immediate_flush": true } }
```
I can apply and roll back quickly.

aj: While that's applied, I'll prepare a minimal runtime fix: clamp the adaptive window max to 300ms for long prompt estimations and add a quick unit test. This will go into hotfix v2.14.1.

devon: Also recommend a temporary rule in requests router to prefer non-adaptive kernels for that tenant if immediate_flush can't be toggled for some routes.

alex: Action items:
- maria: apply tenant override now and report back.
- aj: PR for clamp + tests, target hotfix release today.
- devon: prepare rollback plan for streaming canary if hotfix not possible within 3 hours.
- samir: share repro curl + customer timeline with eng when done.

maria: done — override applied at 2025-11-03T15:12:09Z (control-plane id cp-78910). I can see first_chunk latency drop to baseline in dashboards for acmepay.

srebot: [deploy-bot] control-plane:tenant-override applied by maria (cp-78910).

samir: Customer confirms latency improved in their staging tests. They want a permanent fix and postmortem.

aj: opened PR #4237 with clamp + regression test. CI passing locally, requesting review from @maria and @devon. Plan: canary hotfix to 10% streaming traffic for 30m, run smoke tests for first_chunk latency, then full rollout.

devon: Can we add a monitoring alert to detect recurring regressions? Suggest an alert on 5m increase of p99_streaming_first_chunk > 400ms over baseline for any tenant for >10m.

alex: I'll create the support ticket and update the customer with mitigation and timeline + will request postmortem once hotfix deploys.

maria: postmortem notes — root cause: adaptive coalescing window estimation used an outdated token emission model for long prompt distributions; under certain sequences it grew the flush window too large. Fix: clamp window + improve estimator; mitigation: per-tenant override + quick alerting rule.

aj: I'll add telemetry (a debug flag) to log adaptive window size decisions for canary so we can validate behavior in prod without verbose logging for all tenants.

alex: thanks team. Samir, update customer: workaround applied, hotfix in progress, monitoring/alerting plan, postmortem to follow. :thumbsup:

samir: will do. closing the escalated channel once hotfix verified by customer.
